key_insight: Strong benchmark performance did not ensure reliable cross-dataset predictions, and source-fitted temperature scaling increased confidence in errors.
clinical_relevance: Chest X-ray AI may become less accurate and misleadingly confident when transferred between hospital datasets, supporting cross-site validation before deployment.
method: Trained ResNet-50 and DenseNet-121 on CheXpert; evaluated transfer to MIMIC-CXR for pneumothorax and pleural effusion.
Measured AUC, ECE, Brier score, and average confidence on incorrect predictions with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.
Tested source-validation temperature scaling and examined attention patterns using Grad-CAM.
evidence_signal: Across five experimental settings, cross-domain AUC fell 7–13 percentage points, while temperature scaling increased confidence on errors in all four model–pathology combinations.
watch_item: Evidence covers two architectures, two findings, and one dataset-transfer direction; broader clinical generalizability remains uncertain.
paper_title: When Should We Trust Medical Image Models? Evaluating Confidence Reliability under Cross-Dataset Shift
